attempted_axis: Re-screen of DrawGlowText's OPERAND_DIFF residual against the current corpus: multiply operand order, extern-vs-in-TU definition of the glow globals, and adoption of real names for the five lbl_* sdata/sbss labels it reads. Residual reduced to ONE named mechanism.

attributes.axis_log: AXIS-A multiply operand order: target emits `mullw r0,r0,r3` (quotient,divisor) and ours `mullw r0,r9,r0` (divisor,quotient); rewriting the source as `phase -= divisor * (load / divisor)` was byte-NEUTRAL - MWCC canonicalises commutative integer operands, so the operand order is NOT source-controllable and is a symptom of the register choice, not a cause. AXIS-B extern-vs-definition: these globals live inside btext's own .sdata/.sbss pool but the reconstruction declares them `extern` with no definition anywhere in the tree; defining them in-TU with their real initialisers (glow_color 0x008200EA, glow_radius 40, glow_period 5, glow_font 6, read from build/GUNE5D/asm/auto_09_80343B18_sdata.s) was byte-NEUTRAL, so undefined-extern vs local-definition is not a codegen lever here. AXIS-C symbol naming: symbols.txt still carried lbl_80343BC4/BCC/BD0/BD4 while the source asserted glow_color/glow_radius/glow_period/glow_font, so every one of those relocations diffed on NAME alone; adopted via gdlmem.py rename-symbol --apply (commit 096cfc4ee).

attributes.law_screen: Full corpus screen returned NOTHING for this mechanism: `laws --query "saved register"`, `laws --query "temp register"`, `search "scratch register allocation order volatile"` and `search "temporary register order divisor"` are all silent, so no existing law covers MWCC's volatile/scratch allocation direction. claim.law.chained-init-constant-share.20260829.v1 screened, not applicable - no shared-constant pair in this block. claim.law.hoisted-literal-temp-colors-below-parameter-homes.20260831.v1 (proposed this session) screened, not applicable - the whole residual block is integer, with no FP pool constant involved. claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule.20260830.v1 screened - declaration timing is on the prior record's do-not-retry list and the instruction ORDER already matches target exactly, so there is no entry-schedule gap to close. claim.law.pool-literal-sweep-section-and-lvalue-preconditions.20260831.v1 applied to the naming work (verified glow_* are .sdata, and deliberately did NOT rename lbl_80343BC8, a 0.33f consumed by options.c). Prior do-not-retry list from v1 honoured and not re-run: remainder owner, signedness, declaration order, inline divisor, radius cache, register hint.
attributes.residual: ONE mechanism, REGISTER_ONLY: the scratch-register allocation DIRECTION over the five pre-call temporaries of the phase computation. Target allocates DESCENDING from r8 and drops the shortest-lived value into r3 - radius r8, period r0, span r7, load r6, divisor r3. Ours allocates ASCENDING from r6 - radius r6, period r0, span r7, load r8, divisor r9. Both agree on period=r0 and span=r7; the whole real-16 count is the 8 instructions at fn+0x24..0x40 plus the fn+0x54 compare, with identical opcodes, identical order and identical immediates. Two relocation lines (sBTextOne, sBTextIntBias) are MWCC-generated .sdata2 literals - the int-to-double bias 0x4330000080000000 is emitted by the (f32) cast expansion itself and is not source-reachable; both were confirmed unscored by objdiff.
